device_scope: GT-BE19000AI BCM6813 / Brahma-B53 only; the separate AI board needs its own target profile
profile_status: Future userspace build inputs; not connected to the current firmware build
current_userspace_policy: Preserve stock non-module rootfs content until kernel acceptance is complete; userspace fixtures may be used inside disposable QEMU tests

cpu_policy.isa: ARMv8.0-A plus CRC and Crypto, FP/NEON
cpu_policy.distribution_minimum_cpu_baseline: Do not inherit generic Debian/Ubuntu armel or armhf CPU flags for our rebuilt components
cpu_policy.note: Tuning alias does not change hardware identity; crypto flags permit instructions but do not automatically rewrite algorithms

armel.role: Current BCM SDK 32-bit ASUS userspace uses armel/softfp; retain this ABI for rebuilt components and links to its vendor objects

armhf.role: Optional compatibility target for additional armhf components installed in the future; not a dependency of the current BCM SDK
armhf.activation: Provide its loader and matching runtime libraries when an additional component requires armhf; do not migrate current SDK components to armhf

arm64.role: Default for new and successfully ported userspace components without incompatible vendor dependencies

linkage_rules: Each enabled ABI gets its own sysroot, loader, libc, libgcc and required libstdc++; armhf runtime provisioning is optional until an added component needs it
Do not link or dlopen armel, armhf and arm64 objects across ABI boundaries; communicate between processes when needed
Closed-source binaries retain their original ABI; rebuilding ASUS components as armel applies where source and link-compatible dependencies are available
Native 64-bit vendor userspace blobs remain 64-bit unless their source can be rebuilt
All kernel modules remain AArch64 and follow kernel Kbuild flags; userspace FP/NEON flags are not kernel CFLAGS
kernel_acceptance: Retain CONFIG_COMPAT and CONFIG_COMPAT_BINFMT_ELF for native AArch32 execution
For new syscalls/backports validate arm64 and applicable AArch32 compat entry points, structure translation, signals and error behavior
Run unchanged modern systemd and cgroup-v2 workloads in disposable QEMU; systemd 262 currently fails on kernel #6
Check vendor ABI layouts and regression-test retained modules
After QEMU passes, verify hardware Wi-Fi, Ethernet/Runner, AiMesh and AI-board connectivity under stock userspace with the original fallback preserved

validation_status.future_target_flags: Preprocessor feature/ABI checks passed on available compilers; no future userspace runtime has been built or installed by this check
validation_status.gcc16_for_arm32: Not established by these checks; the existing BE98 ARM32 compiler is GCC 13.3.0

vendor_sdk_context.provenance: Verified by static inspection of official RT-BE92U 102_39063 and 102_40311 firmware plus the current BE19000AI stock-rootfs inventory on 2026-10-03
vendor_sdk_context.current_sdk: The current BE19000AI BCM SDK inventory has zero armhf ELF files; its 32-bit vendor ABI is armel/softfp
vendor_sdk_context.newer_be92_sdk: RT-BE92U 102_40311 changes the boot image SDK identifier from 5.04L.04p3 to 6.2.0, kernel 4.19.294 to 5.15.167, glibc 2.32 to 2.38 and main 32-bit ASUS userspace from armel/softfp to armhf; a few shipped legacy exceptions remain
vendor_sdk_context.scope: Keep the newer BE92 SDK migration separate from optional armhf compatibility in this project; its image targets BCM6765, not BCM6813
